questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.explanation: Article 124 of the Constitution establishes the Supreme Court of India and prescribes the appointment and qualifications of the Chief Justice and judges. (Article 214 deals with High Courts).
questions.citation: Constitution of India — Part V, Chapter IV

questions.question: In macroeconomic accounting, Gross National Product at factor cost (GNP_FC) is equal to:
options: GNP at market price minus Net Indirect Taxes (Indirect Taxes - Subsidies)
GDP at market price plus Net Indirect Taxes
NNP at factor cost plus Net Factor Income from Abroad
GDP at factor cost minus Depreciation
questions.explanation: Market Price includes Net Indirect Taxes. Therefore: Factor Cost = Market Price - Net Indirect Taxes (Taxes - Subsidies). Thus GNP_FC = GNP_MP - Net Indirect Taxes.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics — National Income Accounting

questions.question: Which of the following chemical compounds is commonly known as 'Plaster of Paris'?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris (POP) is chemically Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate with the formula CaSO₄·½H₂O (or 2CaSO₄·H₂O). It is manufactured by heating Gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) to 373 K (100°C) in a kiln. Reaction: CaSO₄·2H₂O —(373 K)→ CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O. If heated above 393 K, all water of crystallization is lost, forming anhydrous calcium sulphate ('dead burnt plaster'), which no longer sets rapidly with water.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Science — Chapter 2 Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.question: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, popularly known as the 'Anti-Defection Law', was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule of the Constitution of India, popularly termed the 'Anti-Defection Law', was introduced by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1985 under Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. It specifies the criteria for disqualifying legislators who voluntarily resign from their political party or defy party whips during voting. The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 strengthened this by eliminating the one-third split protection clause.
questions.citation: Constitution of India — Tenth Schedule

questions.question: Which high mountain pass connects the Kashmir Valley with the Union Territory of Ladakh through the Zaskar Range?
questions.explanation: Zoji La (Zojila Pass) is a high-altitude mountain pass located at approximately 3,528 metres (11,575 feet) above sea level in the Himalayan Zaskar range. It serves as the primary gateway on National Highway 1 (NH-1) connecting Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley with Drass, Kargil, and Leh in Ladakh. Construction of the 14.15 km bi-directional Zojila Tunnel aims to ensure round-the-year, all-weather connectivity across the pass.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 11 India Physical Environment — Mountain Passes

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) located?
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations (UN). Established in June 1945 by the UN Charter, it began operations in April 1946. It is seated at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. Crucially, of the six principal UN organs, the ICJ is the only one not headquartered in New York City. It consists of 15 independent judges elected for 9-year terms by the UN General Assembly and Security Council.
questions.citation: United Nations System — Principal Organs

questions.question: In which medium does sound travel with the highest velocity at 25°C?
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave requiring elastic matter to propagate. Because solids have the highest elastic bulk modulus and density coupling, sound travels fastest in solid metals (~6,420 m/s in aluminium), followed by liquids (~1,498 m/s in water), gases (~346 m/s in air), and 0 m/s in vacuum.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 9 Science — Chapter 12 Sound

questions.question: Which planet in our solar system has the shortest orbital period around the Sun (88 Earth days)?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the smallest and innermost planet in our solar system, orbiting the Sun at an average distance of roughly 0.387 astronomical units (57.9 million km). In accordance with Kepler's Third Law of Planetary Motion (T² ∝ a³), Mercury has the shortest orbital period of any planet, completing one full revolution around the Sun in just 87.97 Earth days at an average orbital speed of 47.36 km/s.
questions.citation: Physical Geography — Planetary Motions

questions.question: The renowned treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy titled 'Arthashastra' is traditionally attributed to:
questions.explanation: The 'Arthashastra' is an ancient Indian Sanskrit manual on statecraft, economic policy, state administration, and military strategy. It is traditionally credited to Kautilya (also identified as Vishnugupta or Chanakya), who served as the chief advisor and prime minister to Emperor Chandragupta Maurya (c. 321–297 BCE). The text is organized into 15 books (Adhikaranas) and 150 chapters detailing fiscal policy, trade, law, and diplomacy.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Indian History — Early States and Economies

questions.question: What is the chemical name of common baking soda?
questions.explanation: Common baking soda is chemically known as Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate or Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO₃). It is manufactured industrially through the Solvay process: NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃. In comparison: Washing soda is Sodium Carbonate Decahydrate (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O); Caustic soda is Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH); and Bleaching powder is Calcium Oxychloride (CaOCl₂). During baking, NaHCO₃ thermally decomposes to release CO₂ bubbles.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Science — Chapter 2 Baking Soda
